stories.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
summary: A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature.

Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing room-temperature superconductivity.

stories.title: Stormont department failing to protect wild birds, investigation finds
summary: The Office for Environmental Protection said Daera had not complied with environmental law requiring it to classify and update Special Protection Areas.

stories.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age.
The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
Surprisingly, some older adults retain the same powerful cleansing waves seen in younger people.

stories.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
summary: Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease that could open the door to new treatments.

By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice.
Removing the protein made the damage worse, highlighting its critical protective role.

stories.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world.

New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.

summary: The BBC looks at why in a dry summer with few sewage spills, one bathing site failed so many water quality tests.

stories.title: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
summary: Deep-sea researchers have captured stunning new footage of an extraordinarily rare fish with a transparent head and rotating eyes nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface.
Known as the barreleye fish, this bizarre creature uses its upward-pointing eyes to spot prey before rotating them forward to track its next meal, all while a transparent dome protects them.

stories.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
summary: A remarkable 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia reveals that early humans once thrived beside enormous lakes filled with wildlife in what is now a vast desert.
Thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains suggest these prehistoric people used sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially including weapons enhanced with poisonous plant compounds.

stories.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
summary: Scientists discovered that although people with and without autism show surprisingly similar average brain activity, individuals with autism exhibit much greater differences from one another, especially in regions involved in social understanding.
The findings suggest that traditional research methods may be overlooking crucial differences that could help unlock more personalized autism support.
